kentat: ### What did I do, and how?
### Why did I do it this way?

36.otsikko: GDD into tasks, project set up

tehtavat.teksti: Write a question list from the brief and your GDD
tehtavat.valmis: The question list covers the gaps between the brief and the GDD, and every question is either answered or marked open.
tehtavat.tallenna: The question list in `project-docs/`. The open items go into the week 36 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Scope P0 with your instructor and break it into issues
tehtavat.valmis: The P0 scope is agreed with your instructor and recorded in the plan, and every piece of P0 is an issue draft with a done-when condition.
tehtavat.tallenna: The P0 scope and who approved it in the plan and in the week 36 journal entry. The drafts become GitHub issues in work step 3.

tehtavat.teksti: Set up the Unity project in a public GitHub repository
tehtavat.valmis: A fresh clone of the repository opens in Unity without errors by following the README alone, and the milestone "MVP 4 Dec" holds the P0 issues.
tehtavat.tallenna: Commit and push. The repository address and the hash of the first commit go into the week 36 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Name the game team and hold the first weekly meeting
tehtavat.valmis: The meeting note lists the attendees by role and the agreements with issue numbers, and the implementation plan is in `project-docs/`.
tehtavat.tallenna: `project-docs/meetings/week36.md` and `project-docs/gdd-implementation-plan.md`, committed and pushed. People appear in the repository only by role; if your instructor needs the names, send them in Teams.

36.nayta: A public repository whose README, P0 milestone and first commit say what is being built — plus the question list with answers and the meeting note in project-docs.
36.tuotos: A public GitHub repository, a P0 milestone with issues, a question list for the client, the GDD and the implementation plan in project-docs, and the first weekly meeting note.
36.valmis: An outsider can see from the repository what is being built and in which order: the README describes the game in one paragraph, the milestone "MVP 4 Dec" holds the P0 issues, and the project compiles as an empty scene.
36.label: 31 Aug – 4 Sep

37.otsikko: Tanks move — two players, one keyboard

tehtavat.teksti: Build the tank prefab and place two tanks in a test arena
tehtavat.valmis: One tank prefab exists, and two instances of it in different colours stand in a walled test arena that the camera shows whole.
tehtavat.tallenna: The prefab and the scene, committed with a message that names the issue.

tehtavat.teksti: Move two tanks with physics on one keyboard
tehtavat.valmis: Both tanks move at the same time on one keyboard without disturbing each other, and they stop at walls without jittering.
tehtavat.tallenna: Small commits that name the issue, for example "Tank movement: two players, one keyboard (#3)". Your input and Rigidbody2D settings go into the week 37 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Run test cases T01–T02 and hold the weekly meeting
tehtavat.valmis: T01 and T02 each have an expected result written before the run and an actual result, and the meeting note is in the repository.
tehtavat.tallenna: `project-docs/tests.md` and `project-docs/meetings/week37.md`, committed. The results of T01–T02 go into the week 37 journal entry.

37.nayta: A playable build with two tanks moving, test cases T01–T02 with results in tests.md, and the movement commits.
37.tuotos: A tank prefab (square body + round turret per the GDD), two-player input mapping (WASD / arrows), Rigidbody2D-based movement, a fixed test arena. 2 recorded test cases.
37.valmis: Two players can move at the same time on one keyboard without the keys interfering with each other, and the tanks stop at a wall without jittering.
37.label: 7–11 Sep

tehtavat.teksti: Build the bouncing Projectile prefab
tehtavat.valmis: The Projectile prefab has Bounciness 1 and Friction 0 on the shell and on the walls, Linear Drag 0 and continuous collision detection.
tehtavat.tallenna: The Projectile prefab, committed with a message that names the issue. The physics material settings go into the week 38 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Let each player fire one shell at a time
tehtavat.valmis: Each player can fire only when their previous shell is gone, and the shell leaves the barrel slightly faster than the tank moves.
tehtavat.tallenna: `TankShooting.cs`, committed with a message that names the issue. How you limited it to one shell goes into the week 38 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Make shells despawn after ~10 s and destroy any tank they hit
tehtavat.valmis: A shell disappears after about 10 seconds, and a hit destroys any tank, including the one that fired it.
tehtavat.tallenna: `Projectile.cs`, committed with a message that names the issue.

tehtavat.teksti: Run test cases T03–T05 and playtest the ricochet
tehtavat.valmis: T03–T05 each have an expectation written before the run and an actual result, and the ricochet feedback is in the meeting note.
tehtavat.tallenna: `tests.md` and `meetings/week38.md` committed, with a short video or image sequence of the ricocheting shell in `project-docs/`. The results go into the week 38 journal entry.

38.nayta: A video or image sequence of the ricocheting shell, test cases T03–T05 with results, and the Projectile prefab commit.
38.tuotos: A Projectile prefab and shooting for both players: one shell per player on the field, ricochet through a physics material, despawn on a timer. 3 recorded test cases.
38.valmis: The shell bounces off walls without losing speed, disappears in about 10 seconds, kills its own shooter too, and a new shell can only be fired once the previous one is gone.
38.label: 14–18 Sep

39.otsikko: Rounds, scoring and the five-second rule

tehtavat.teksti: Destroy a hit tank and clean up the round
tehtavat.valmis: A hit tank disappears with an effect and no longer reacts to its keys, and no shells are left on the field when the round ends.
tehtavat.tallenna: Commits that name the issue.

tehtavat.teksti: Score rounds with the five-second rule and restart them
tehtavat.valmis: Rounds end, score and restart without touching the editor, and two deaths within 5 s give no point.
tehtavat.tallenna: The GameManager, committed with a message that names the issue. How you built the 5 s rule and stored the scores goes into the week 39 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Run test cases T06–T08 and play rounds with the game team
tehtavat.valmis: T06–T08 have expectations written before the run and actual results, and the meeting note judges the round rhythm.
tehtavat.tallenna: `tests.md` and `meetings/week39.md`, committed. The results of T06–T08 go into the week 39 journal entry.

39.nayta: scoring, the 5 s rule tested (T06–T08) and the playtest note week39.md.
39.tuotos: GameManager: tank destruction, scoring, the 5 s rule, round restart, a score display at the top of the screen — the first version of the HUD, the heads-up display drawn on top of the running match. 3 recorded test cases.
39.valmis: A whole round works without touching the editor: destruction, a point to the right player (or to neither, under the 5 s rule), and an automatic new round.
39.label: 21–25 Sep

40.otsikko: Generated maze and data out of the code

tehtavat.teksti: Compare the data stores before you implement anything
tehtavat.valmis: The comparison covers all three options, names the store chosen for arena and power-up data with its reason, and was written before the maze code.
tehtavat.tallenna: The comparison in the GitHub issue or the journal. The choice and its reasoning in the plan (`project-docs/gdd-implementation-plan.md`).

tehtavat.teksti: Write the depth-first search (DFS) maze generator
tehtavat.valmis: The generator produces a 10×10 maze in which every cell is visited, and you can explain each step of it from your paper drawing.
tehtavat.tallenna: `MazeGenerator.cs` committed, and a photo of the paper drawing in `project-docs/`. Explain the DFS in your own words in the week 40 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Build the arena from data with fair spawn positions
tehtavat.valmis: Changing the arena size in the data changes the maze without any code change, the tanks always start at least 3 tiles apart, and every round starts in a newly generated maze.
tehtavat.tallenna: `MazeBuilder.cs` and the arena data, committed. The distance measure goes into the week 40 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Run test cases T09–T10 for traversability and spawn distance
tehtavat.valmis: T09 and T10 have expectations written before the run, a stated way of verifying and actual results.
tehtavat.tallenna: `project-docs/tests.md` committed, with screenshots of generated mazes. The results of T09–T10 go into the week 40 journal entry.

40.nayta: The written data store comparison, the paper drawing of the depth-first search, generated mazes and test cases T09–T10.
40.tuotos: MazeGenerator (DFS), 10×10 working (5×5 and 25×25 as P1 issues), a new maze every round, spawn validation, arena configuration in a ScriptableObject or JSON + a written data store comparison. 2 recorded test cases.
40.valmis: Every generated 10×10 maze is fully traversable (DFS guarantees it), the tanks start at least 3 tiles apart, and the arena size is read from data — you can change the size without touching code — and every round starts in a newly generated maze.
40.label: 28 Sep – 2 Oct

tehtavat.teksti: Define the three power-ups as data
tehtavat.valmis: Three power-ups are defined as data with their durations and effects, and no power has its own if branch in the code.
tehtavat.tallenna: The power-up data in your chosen store (for example the `PowerUpData` script and three assets in `Assets/Data/PowerUps/`), committed. Why data and not code goes into the week 41 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Spawn power-ups and apply one power at a time
tehtavat.valmis: Power-ups appear about every 2 seconds at the centres of free tiles, a player holds at most one power, and every effect ends on time.
tehtavat.tallenna: The spawner, pickup and runner scripts, committed with messages that name the issue. How you timed the effects goes into the week 41 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Show active powers in the HUD and run test cases T11–T12
tehtavat.valmis: A spectator can see both players' powers from the HUD and the tanks, and T11–T12 have expectations and actual results.
tehtavat.tallenna: A HUD screenshot and `tests.md`, committed. The results of T11–T12 go into the week 41 journal entry.

41.nayta: Three power-up assets as data, a HUD screenshot and test cases T11–T12 with results.
41.tuotos: The power-up system: spawning (~2 s interval, only into free normal tiles), pickup, one power at a time (GDD), duration timers, a HUD icon and a tank indicator. Speed +20 %/10 s, slowness −20 %/10 s on the opponent, shield 15 s or one hit. 2 recorded test cases.
41.valmis: Three powers work with their durations, a player can only hold one at a time (a new one is not picked up before the old one is spent — GDD), and a spectator can see both players' state from the HUD.
41.label: 5–9 Oct

tehtavat.teksti: Demo the playable build and let the client play it
tehtavat.valmis: The client has played the build themselves, and their comments are written down word for word.
tehtavat.tallenna: The quotes go into the review note in work step 2. What you demonstrated and how goes into the week 43 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Write the review note with the client's words kept apart
tehtavat.valmis: The note has the client's quotes and your interpretation in separate parts, and part 2 ends with your proposal.
tehtavat.tallenna: `project-docs/reviews/week43.md`, committed. The client's most important comment goes into the week 43 journal entry as a quote.

tehtavat.teksti: Decide the priorities with the game team and update the plan
tehtavat.valmis: A named decision says what gets built in week 44 and what moves to P1 or P2, and your instructor has signed it off.
tehtavat.tallenna: The decision in the review note and in the updated `project-docs/gdd-implementation-plan.md`, plus `meetings/week43.md`. The reasoning and what you left out go into the week 43 journal entry.

43.nayta: The review note in the client's words, the recorded prioritisation decision and the updated implementation plan.
43.tuotos: A review note (the client's words kept separate from your interpretation), the game team's prioritisation decision from the P1 list (laser / triple shot / special tiles / audio — the chosen one must fit roughly 2 working days), and an updated implementation plan.
43.valmis: The note holds the client's own words, your interpretation separately, and a named decision: what gets built in week 44, what moves to P1/P2. The instructor has signed off on the decision.
43.label: 19–23 Oct

44.otsikko: Feedback change and the chosen extra feature

tehtavat.teksti: Make the feedback change on a branch and open a pull request
tehtavat.valmis: An open pull request to main holds only the feedback change, and its description makes clear which feedback it answers.
tehtavat.tallenna: The pull request in GitHub. Its number and the feedback it resolves go into the week 44 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Build the feature chosen in the review on the existing systems
tehtavat.valmis: The chosen feature works in a real match and uses the existing shell or power-up code.
tehtavat.tallenna: Commits that name the feature's issue. How the feature leans on the week 38 or 41 systems goes into the week 44 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Run a game team playtest and record a shared assessment
tehtavat.valmis: The playtest note holds at least three observations and a shared assessment.
tehtavat.tallenna: `project-docs/meetings/week44-playtest.md`, committed. The main findings go into the week 44 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Run test cases T13–T14 and merge the reviewed pull request
tehtavat.valmis: T13–T14 have expectations and actual results, and main holds the merged pull request with its review comment.
tehtavat.tallenna: `tests.md` and `meetings/week44.md` committed; the merged pull request in GitHub. The results of T13–T14 go into the week 44 journal entry.

44.nayta: A merged PR that references the feedback, the playable feature, the playtest note and test cases T13–T14.
44.tuotos: A PR: the feedback change (branch → main) whose description references the review note; the chosen feature (e.g. triple shot) playable; the game team's playtest note with a shared assessment. 2 recorded test cases.
44.valmis: Main holds a merged PR whose description makes clear which feedback it answers; the feature works; the playtest note holds at least three shared observations and a shared assessment.
44.label: 26–30 Oct

tehtavat.teksti: Complete the test matrix from the GDD's testing list
tehtavat.valmis: The matrix has at least 12 test cases, each with an expectation written before the run, in roughly equal thirds of normal, boundary and error cases.
tehtavat.tallenna: `project-docs/tests.md`, committed.

tehtavat.teksti: Run every test case again and record each result
tehtavat.valmis: Every row of the matrix has a dated result, and T01–T14 have been run again this week.
tehtavat.tallenna: `tests.md`, committed. A summary of the matrix (how many OK, how many fixed) goes into the week 45 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Solve one bug with a debugging pair
tehtavat.valmis: The pair note holds both roles, both sets of observations, the breakpoints and the cause of the bug.
tehtavat.tallenna: The pair note in `project-docs/`, committed. What pair debugging showed about your own way of hunting bugs goes into the week 45 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Finish three complete debugging chains
tehtavat.valmis: Three chains in `project-docs/chains/` each have all six parts, or you have raised the lack of real bugs with your instructor.
tehtavat.tallenna: `project-docs/chains/` and `meetings/week45.md`, committed. The hardest bug and its cause go into the week 45 journal entry.

45.nayta: The run test matrix (≥12 rows), three complete debugging chains and the pair debugging note.
45.tuotos: A run test matrix (≥12 test cases: normal / boundary / error in roughly equal thirds), 3 complete debugging chains, a debugging pair note, regression tests for the fixed bugs.
45.valmis: Every row of the matrix has an expectation recorded before the run and the result of the run; the three chains hold an observation, reproduction steps, the cause, the fix commit, a retest and a regression test; the pair note holds both roles and both sets of observations.
45.label: 2–6 Nov

tehtavat.teksti: Build the main menu and the pause menu
tehtavat.valmis: A player can start a match, pause it, restart it and quit from the menus without touching the editor.
tehtavat.tallenna: The menu and pause commits, with messages that name the issues. The scene or overlay decision goes into the week 46 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Save the settings and block duplicate tank colours
tehtavat.valmis: The settings are still there after the game is closed and opened again, and the same colour cannot be picked twice.
tehtavat.tallenna: Commits that name the issues. What you save to PlayerPrefs and why goes into the week 46 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Run test cases T15–T16 for saved settings and colours
tehtavat.valmis: T15 and T16 have expectations written before the run and actual results.
tehtavat.tallenna: `tests.md`, committed. The results of T15–T16 go into the week 46 journal entry.

46.nayta: The playable menu path, PlayerPrefs settings persistence (T15) and the duplicate colour block (T16).
46.tuotos: Main menu, options (arena size, player colours without duplicates; audio sliders only if audio was chosen in week 43), pause (resume / restart / quit), settings saved to PlayerPrefs. 2 recorded test cases.
46.valmis: The game can be started, the settings changed and a match paused without touching the editor; the settings are still there on the next launch; the same player colour cannot be picked twice.
46.label: 9–13 Nov

47.otsikko: Release candidate, external testing and security

tehtavat.teksti: Build release candidate v1.0-rc1 and test it yourself
tehtavat.valmis: `v1.0-rc1` starts from a clean folder and a whole match can be played in it.
tehtavat.tallenna: The RC build settings go into the week 47 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Write the installation and gameplay guide
tehtavat.valmis: Someone who has never seen the game can find in the guide how to download, start and play it.
tehtavat.tallenna: The guide, committed to the repository.

tehtavat.teksti: Let an outside tester start the game from the guide alone
tehtavat.valmis: The tester got through a whole match without spoken help, and every hesitation is on a fix list for the guide.
tehtavat.tallenna: The test note in `project-docs/`, committed. Where the tester hesitated and how you fixed the guide go into the week 47 journal entry. If your instructor needs the tester's name or exact words, send them in Teams.

tehtavat.teksti: Review your repository's security with exact references
tehtavat.valmis: The security review names the files and commits it checked and what it found.
tehtavat.tallenna: The review in `project-docs/` (for example `security-review.md`), committed. Its findings go into the week 47 journal entry.

47.nayta: The RC build, the written guide, the tester's findings by role and the security review with references.
47.tuotos: An RC build, an installation and gameplay guide, the outside tester's observations (role, date and every hesitation, in your own words), and a security review of your own repository with concrete references.
47.valmis: The tester got all the way through a match without spoken help; every point where they hesitated is recorded as a fix list for the guide; the security review names the files and commits it checked. After the RC, only blocking bugs get fixed.
47.label: 16–20 Nov

tehtavat.teksti: Fix only blocking bugs and update the guide
tehtavat.valmis: Every blocking bug on the fix list is fixed and every guide fix is in the guide, and nothing else has changed.
tehtavat.tallenna: Commits that name the fixes they make.

tehtavat.teksti: Publish release v1.0 with the build and its scope description
tehtavat.valmis: Release v1.0 is public with its build files, and its description separates what the MVP contains from what was left out.
tehtavat.tallenna: The release link goes into the week 48 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Test the release in a clean environment and freeze the content
tehtavat.valmis: The release plays on a clean machine by the guide, the README matches the GDD's controls and rules, and the content freeze commit exists.
tehtavat.tallenna: The clean-environment report, the README and the LICENSE, committed. The LICENSE decision and what ended up as follow-up or optional (P1/P2) go into the week 48 journal entry.

48.nayta: GitHub Release v1.0, the clean-environment test report and the final README + LICENSE.
48.tuotos: GitHub Release v1.0 with the build files (or an itch.io release — the instructor decides), the final README, a LICENSE as agreed, a clean-environment test report, and a content freeze commit.
48.valmis: An outsider can download the release and play a match on a machine that has never had the project on it; the README matches the GDD's controls and rules; the release page states what the MVP contains and what was deliberately left out (P1/P2).
48.label: 23–27 Nov

tehtavat.teksti: Finish the project documentation with exact references
tehtavat.valmis: Every claim in the documentation has at least one exact reference, and anything missing is marked as missing.
tehtavat.tallenna: `project-docs/` with the journal and the AI log, committed.

tehtavat.teksti: Rehearse and time the 8–10 minute demo
tehtavat.valmis: The demo stays within 8–10 minutes and covers the technique, a bug fix and the Git history.
tehtavat.tallenna: The structure of the demo goes into the week 49 journal entry.

tehtavat.teksti: Write the self-assessment and hand over on Fri 4 Dec
tehtavat.valmis: The self-assessment refers to real meeting notes, and the client has received the MVP and the project documentation.
tehtavat.tallenna: The self-assessment in `project-docs/`, committed. Its main points go into the week 49 journal entry.

49.nayta: The finished project documentation, the collected journal and AI log, and the self-assessment in project-docs.
49.tuotos: The collected project journal and AI log in project-docs, a rehearsed 8–10 minute demo, a self-assessment written against the meeting notes, and the handover on Friday 4 December.
49.valmis: Every claim in the documentation has at least one exact reference (commit, test id, note, release); the demo stays inside its time and covers the technique, a bug fix and the Git history; the self-assessment references real meeting notes.
49.label: 30 Nov – 4 Dec
